title: Studying in Germany or New Zealand: a comparison
description: Tuition, living costs, visa rules, work rights and life after graduation compared for the two destinations.
html:
Germany and New Zealand attract many of the same applicants: students who want a good degree in English, a safe country and a realistic path to working afterwards. The two countries differ sharply on cost and on what happens after graduation. Here is a side-by-side view.

Why study abroad at all

A degree abroad brings a second language, a wider network and experience of working across cultures, which employers in every country value. The choice of destination shapes what you pay and what you can do afterwards, so it deserves as much thought as the choice of subject.

Tuition

Public universities in Germany charge no tuition to international students in most states, only a semester contribution of a few hundred euros. In New Zealand, international students pay full tuition, typically NZ$25,000 to NZ$45,000 a year.

Living costs

Germany requires proof of about €11,900 a year and that is close to what a student actually spends outside Munich. New Zealand requires proof of NZ$20,000 a year, and Auckland rents push real costs higher.

Language

New Zealand is English-speaking throughout. Germany offers hundreds of English-taught programmes, mostly at master's level, but daily life benefits from German.

Work during and after studies

Both countries allow part-time work of around 20 hours a week during term. After graduation, Germany grants 18 months to find a job and a straightforward route to a work permit and permanent residence. New Zealand's post-study work visa depends on the level of the qualification and has been tightened in recent years.

Distance and climate

Germany is in the middle of Europe, with cheap travel to neighbouring countries; New Zealand is remote and flights home are long and expensive. The climate is the reverse: mild and green in New Zealand, four real seasons in Germany.

The verdict

On cost and on the path to a career in the country, Germany is hard to beat. New Zealand wins on language convenience and lifestyle. For most students whose budget matters, the free tuition and the 18-month post-study window decide it.
